title: 1.7 Electronic Configurations and Orbital Diagrams
description: Aufbau principle, Pauli exclusion principle, Hund's rule, ground-state electron configurations, and orbital diagrams

questions.question: The distribution of electrons among atomic orbitals in any atom is governed by which three principles?
options: Aufbau (building up) principle, Hund's rule, and Pauli's exclusion principle
conservation of mass, definite proportions, and multiple proportions
Bohr's model, the quantum condition, and the uncertainty principle
questions.correctAnswer: Aufbau (building up) principle, Hund's rule, and Pauli's exclusion principle

questions.question: The Aufbau (building up) principle states that electrons occupy:
options: the lowest-energy orbital available before entering higher-energy orbitals
all orbitals of equal energy simultaneously
questions.correctAnswer: the lowest-energy orbital available before entering higher-energy orbitals

questions.question: According to the Aufbau principle, the ground state subshells are filled in the order $1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, \dots$. Which subshell is filled immediately after 3p?
In the Aufbau filling order, which subshell comes right after 4s?
Hund's rule states that equal-energy (degenerate) orbitals are:
options: each occupied by a single electron before pairing of electrons of opposite spin occurs
filled with two electrons at a time from the start
left empty until all lower levels are full
questions.correctAnswer: each occupied by a single electron before pairing of electrons of opposite spin occurs

questions.question: Pauli's exclusion principle states that no two electrons in an atom can:
options: have the same four quantum numbers
questions.correctAnswer: have the same four quantum numbers

questions.question: Because of the Pauli exclusion principle, two electrons occupying the same orbital must:
In the subshell designation $nl^e$ (for example, $1s^2$), the superscript number indicates:
options: the number of electrons in that subshell
questions.correctAnswer: the number of electrons in that subshell

Valence electrons are defined as the electrons:
options: in the outermost principal quantum level of an atom
questions.correctAnswer: in the outermost principal quantum level of an atom

questions.question: Core electrons are best described as:
options: the inner electrons of an atom that are not in the outermost shell
the electrons in the outermost shell
questions.correctAnswer: the inner electrons of an atom that are not in the outermost shell

questions.question: In an orbital diagram, an upward arrow ($\uparrow$) conventionally represents an electron with:
The three orbitals in the 2p sublevel are described as:
options: degenerate (equal in energy), having the same $n$ and $\ell$ values
capable of holding six electrons each
questions.correctAnswer: degenerate (equal in energy), having the same $n$ and $\ell$ values

questions.question: Chromium ($Z = 24$) has an observed ground state electron configuration different from the one expected from the simple Aufbau rule. Its observed configuration is:
Copper ($Z = 29$) has an observed ground state electron configuration of $[Ar]4s^1 3d^{10}$. This exception to the Aufbau principle is attributed to:
options: the special stability of a completely filled 3d subshell
the special stability of an empty 4s subshell
an error in the periodic table
the special stability of a half-filled 4p subshell
questions.correctAnswer: the special stability of a completely filled 3d subshell

questions.question: The half-filled $3d^5$ subshell of chromium and the fully filled $3d^{10}$ subshell of copper are believed to:
options: lend special stability to those electron configurations
cause the atoms to lose electrons easily
questions.correctAnswer: lend special stability to those electron configurations
